title: How Oregon's offense has improved under new play caller Jay Johnson
text:
Oregon Football: The Ducks' offense has improved under Jay Johnson Schedule Football Basketball Recruiting Big Ten Sports Newsletter FOOTBALL How Oregon's offense has improved under new play caller Jay Johnson
 Zachary Neel Ducks Wire Nov. 10, 2026, 7:27 a.m. PT It's been a wild college football season for the Oregon Ducks , to say the least.
 After entering the year with national championship expectations, the Ducks turned around and ended up falling out of the top 25 for the first time in several years, and wound up firing their offensive coordinator, Drew Mehringer, after just seven games on the job. It turns out that might have been the right move, though, with Oregon turning things around over the past two weeks and getting back into the mix for the Big Ten title race, and a potential shot at a spot in the College Football Playoff.
 A big reason for that has been the offense, now called by veteran offensive mind Jay Johnson, who has simplified some things and put his players in a chance to have success.
 So, how much better has Oregon's offense been since Mehringer was fired and Johnson took over the play sheet? We broke down the numbers, comparing the first seven weeks (six games) to the last two games that Oregon has played with Johnson on the sticks. It's a small sample size, but it does tell us a bit about what we can expect from the Ducks' offense going forward.
 *Note: All of the following stats and rankings are without the inclusion of numbers from the 84-0 win over Portland State. That game came against an FCS opponent, so they do not register in the national rankings or season-long averages. 
 Love crosswords? Explore the Crossword page and play the new MidGrid Crossword. Scoring
 Points Per Game Under Drew Mehringer: 24.7 (75th nationally)
 --> Points Per Game Under Jay Johnson: 37.5 (10th nationally)
 The scoring is arguably the biggest positive change for Oregon's offense. You could argue that the 24.7 points per game number was even inflated by the non-Power 4 conference games early in the year — Oregon scored 34 and 31 against Boise State and Oklahoma State. In the final three games of Mehringer's tenure, the Ducks put up 15 points, 17 points, and 10 points, respectively.
 By contrast, the Ducks have put up 34 points and 41 points in the two games with Johnson calling plays, a big improvement, albeit in a small sample size.
 Total Offense
 Yards Per Game Under Drew Mehringer: 423.1 (42nd nationally)
 Yards Per Game Under Jay Johnson: 418.0 (30th nationally)
 Oregon's total offense has actually gone down — again, small sample size — since Johnson took over. Part of that is buoyed by a pair of big performances early in the year — 497 yards vs. Boise State, and 504 yards vs. USC — but for the most part, I think it's fair to give Mehringer some credit here. The Oregon offense wasn't always unable to move the ball when he was calling plays, but it was rather an issue of capitalizing in big moments and punching the ball in the endzone when the Ducks got close. I will be interested to revisit this number after we get a larger sample size with Johnson on the headset.
 Passing
 Passing Yards Per Game Under Drew Mehringer: 277.7 (24th nationally)
 Passing Yards Per Game Under Jay Johnson: 311.5 (9th nationally)
 The Ducks have taken a major step forward in this category, largely due to the fact that they are pushing the ball downfield more and straying away from the quick passing game that was leaned on heavily earlier in the year. Dylan Raiola has 12.7 air yards per attempt against Northwestern, and 7.43 against Ohio State, both numbers higher than any game he started with Mehringer as the playcaller. The Ducks are willing to push the ball downfield more and let their playmakers try to make plays. So far, it's working.
 Rushing
 Rushing Yards Per Game Under Drew Mehringer: 145.5 (88th nationally)
 Rushing Yards Per Game Under Jay Johnson: 106.5 (121st nationally)
 Not everything is better under Johnson, to be clear. While Oregon's offensive line has played two of its best games of the season over the past two weeks, the running game has struggled, putting up just 105 and 108 yards. Of course, Oregon's rushing attack was not lethal earlier in the year, so it's not as if this is a major drop-off, but something to note over the next few weeks as we look for a bigger sample size.
 3rd Down Conversions
 3rd Down Conversion % Under Drew Mehringer: 35% (107th nationally)
 3rd Down Conversion % Under Jay Johnson: 45.2% (26th nationally)
 This is an area where Oregon has improved greatly under Jay Johnson. Not only are the Ducks converting more on 3rd down with him as the play caller, but they're converting from farther away, as well. Oregon had four conversions of 3rd and 10 or longer against Ohio State, which is an impressive statistic. Of course, they struggled mightily on 1st down, which led to a whopping 15 instances of 2nd and 10 or longer, which is something that needs to be cleaned up. Regardless, the fact that they are able to move the chains more often is a positive in its own right.
 Red Zone Efficiency
 Red Zone Conversion % Under Drew Mehringer: 93% (17th nationally)
 Red Zone Conversion % Under Jay Johnson: 100% (1st nationally)
 Another percentage that has gone up under Johnson, as the Ducks have been perfect in the redzone so far under his watch. There have been field goals and touchdowns, but most importantly, touchdowns on 4th-and-goal, where the team had to have it. Expecting this to stay at 100% throughout the remainder of the season may be a bit lofty, but as of now, Johnson is pitching a perfect game inside the 20.
